label: Starter Plan: written with AI help and reviewed by a person.

nights.why: Advent begins in the dark, and God's first promise is simple: light is coming.

talk.little: What do you see when all the lights go off?
talk.kids: When have you felt like you were waiting in the dark?
talk.grownups: Where do you most need light this season?

nights.pray: God of light, thank you that the dark does not win. Help us wait for Jesus with hope. Amen.
nights.do: Turn off the lights for one minute and sit together quietly. Then switch on one lamp and say together: light is coming.

nights.why: God's light is not only for looking at. It shines on us so we can shine too.

talk.little: Can you stand up tall and shine like the sun?
talk.kids: What is one way your face can show God's light to someone tomorrow?
talk.grownups: Who has been a light to you, and have you told them?

nights.pray: Jesus, shine on our family so we can shine for others. Amen.
nights.do: Stand in a circle and take turns saying one kind thing about the person on your left.

nights.why: When we feel scared, we can remember who our light is.

talk.little: What helps you feel safe at night?
talk.kids: What is something that makes you afraid, and how could God help?
talk.grownups: What fear have you been carrying that you could hand to God tonight?

nights.pray: Lord, you are our light. When we are afraid, help us remember you are near. Amen.
nights.do: Make a simple night-light promise: each person says one thing they will remember when they feel afraid.

nights.why: A lamp shows the next step, not the whole road. God's word helps us take the next step.

talk.little: Can you take one tiny step and then stop?
talk.kids: What is one choice coming up this week where you need help knowing what to do?
talk.grownups: What next step is God showing you, even if you can't see the whole road?

nights.pray: God, light up the next step for each of us. Help us follow you one step at a time. Amen.
nights.do: With a flashlight, take turns guiding someone across a dim room one step at a time, then switch roles.

nights.why: Even when we fall down or feel sad, God is our light and helps us get back up.

talk.little: What do you do when you fall down?
talk.kids: Tell about a time you made a mistake and got another chance.
talk.grownups: Where do you need to hear that falling is not the end of the story?

nights.pray: Lord, when we fall, help us get up again. Thank you that you never leave us in the dark. Amen.
nights.do: Play a gentle game: everyone sits on the floor and helps someone else stand up. Talk about who helps you get back up.

nights.why: God lights up our lamp. We don't have to make our own light.

talk.little: Who turns on the lights in our house?
talk.kids: What is something hard that God could help you with this week?
talk.grownups: What are you trying to do in your own strength that God wants to help with?

nights.pray: God, thank you for lighting our lamp. Help us trust you with what feels too hard. Amen.
nights.do: A grown-up lights a candle, or use a battery candle. Each person names one hard thing and one way God has helped before.

nights.why: God's light is meant to reach everyone, especially people who feel left out.

talk.little: Who could you share a hug with?
talk.kids: Who at school or church might feel left out, and how could you include them?
talk.grownups: Who in our neighborhood could use some light this month?

nights.pray: God, open our eyes to people who feel alone. Use our family to share your light. Amen.
nights.do: Draw or write a short thank-you note for someone who helps your family, and plan together how to give it.

nights.why: Jesus is called the Prince of Peace. His kind of peace never runs out.

talk.little: What does it feel like to be calm?
talk.kids: Which name for Jesus in this reading do you like most, and why?
talk.grownups: Where do you need the peace that only Jesus gives?

nights.pray: Prince of Peace, quiet our hearts tonight. Make our home a place of your peace. Amen.
nights.do: Take three slow breaths together. On each one, pray quietly: Jesus, give us peace.

nights.why: God dreams of a day when fighting turns into helping. We can practice that now.

talk.little: What can you do when you feel mad?
talk.kids: How can you turn an argument into helping each other?
talk.grownups: Is there someone you need to make peace with?

nights.pray: God, help us choose kind words and gentle hands. Let our home walk in your light. Amen.
nights.do: Think of a recent argument in the family. Together, act out a do-over where it ends with helping instead.

nights.why: Zechariah sang that Jesus would be like the sunrise, guiding our feet into peace.

talk.little: What do you see when the sun comes up?
talk.kids: What is your favorite part of the morning, and why?
talk.grownups: What would it look like for your feet to walk in the way of peace this week?

nights.pray: God, like the sunrise, come into our home. Guide our feet in the way of peace. Amen.
nights.do: Plan to look out a window together at sunrise this week. Tonight, draw a picture of what you hope to see.

nights.why: When our minds stay close to God, our hearts can rest.

talk.little: What do you think about when you go to bed?
talk.kids: What do you do when your mind feels busy or worried?
talk.grownups: What helps you keep your mind on God when life gets noisy?

nights.pray: God, keep our minds close to you. Give us rest and trust tonight. Amen.
nights.do: Each person shares one worry and one thing they trust God for. Then everyone says together: we can rest.

nights.why: We can sleep in peace because God keeps watch over us.

talk.little: Who watches over you when you sleep?
talk.kids: What helps you fall asleep when you feel worried?
talk.grownups: What would help you rest more deeply this Advent?

nights.pray: Lord, thank you for keeping watch over us. Help us lie down and sleep in peace. Amen.
nights.do: Make up a short bedtime blessing together that you can say every night this week.

nights.why: Jesus gives a peace that is different from what the world gives.

talk.little: What makes your heart feel happy and calm?
talk.kids: What is the difference between being quiet and having peace inside?
talk.grownups: What troubles your heart right now that you can bring to Jesus?

nights.pray: Jesus, thank you for your peace. Help our hearts not be troubled or afraid. Amen.
nights.do: Pass a pillow around the table. Whoever holds it shares one thing that helps them feel calm.

nights.why: Isaiah saw a world where even enemies become friends. That is God's peace.

talk.little: Can you roar like a big bear?
talk.kids: If a wolf and a lamb could be friends, what else could change?
talk.grownups: What broken relationship do you hope God will mend?

nights.pray: God, we long for your peace in our world. Make us peacemakers starting at home. Amen.
nights.do: Draw a picture of two animals that would never be friends, now living together in peace.

nights.why: Jesus came with good news that turns sadness into joy.

talk.little: What makes you smile?
talk.kids: What good news would you love to tell someone?
talk.grownups: Where have you seen God turn sorrow into something good?

nights.pray: God of joy, thank you for good news. Comfort anyone who is sad tonight. Amen.
nights.do: Each person shares one piece of good news from today, big or small.

nights.why: Sad nights don't last forever. Joy comes in the morning.

talk.little: What do you like to do when you wake up?
talk.kids: Tell about a time something sad turned out better than you expected.
talk.grownups: How has God met you in a hard season before?

nights.pray: Lord, thank you that sadness does not have the last word. Bring us joy in the morning. Amen.
nights.do: Plan a small happy surprise for breakfast tomorrow, like a drawing at someone's place or a silly song.

nights.why: Mary sang because God did great things for her. We can sing about God's goodness too.

talk.little: What song do you like to sing?
talk.kids: What great thing has God done for our family this year?
talk.grownups: What would your own song of thanks to God include?

nights.pray: God, our hearts praise you. Thank you for the great things you have done for us. Amen.
nights.do: Sing a favorite Christmas song together, or make up a short song of thanks.

nights.why: Joy is like water from a deep well. God never runs dry.

talk.little: Can you act like you pour a cup?
talk.kids: What fills you up when you feel tired or sad?
talk.grownups: Where do you go to draw joy when you feel empty?

nights.pray: God, you are our strength and our song. Fill us with joy that does not run dry. Amen.
nights.do: Pour everyone a glass of water. Before you drink, each person names one thing that fills them with joy.

nights.why: Even before he was born, John jumped for joy when Jesus came near.

talk.little: Can you jump up for joy?
talk.kids: What news would make you jump for joy?
talk.grownups: When did you last feel real joy about Jesus being near?

nights.pray: Jesus, when you come near, our hearts leap. Thank you for being with us. Amen.
nights.do: Have a one-minute joy jump: everyone jumps and calls out one thing they're thankful for.

nights.why: Jesus says he is the light of the world. Following him means we don't walk in darkness.

talk.little: Who can be our light?
talk.kids: What does it mean to follow Jesus at school or with friends?
talk.grownups: Where is Jesus inviting you to follow him more closely?

nights.pray: Jesus, light of the world, help us follow you. Let us never walk alone in the dark. Amen.
nights.do: Play follow the leader around the house with a flashlight. Then talk about what it means to follow Jesus.

nights.why: Jesus says we are the light of the world too, when we let his love shine through us.

talk.little: Can you show me a big smile?
talk.kids: What is one good thing you could do this week that would shine for others?
talk.grownups: How can our family shine together this Christmas?

nights.pray: Jesus, help us shine your light through kind words and good deeds. Amen.
nights.do: Choose one kind act your family can do together this week for a neighbor or friend, and decide on a day.

nights.why: An angel told Mary not to be afraid. God's love was coming to her in a surprising way.

talk.little: What would you say to an angel?
talk.kids: Why do you think the angel said, do not be afraid?
talk.grownups: When has God's love surprised you?

nights.pray: God, thank you for loving us first. Help us say yes to you like Mary did. Amen.
nights.do: Talk about a time you were surprised by love. Then write the words do not be afraid on a paper for the fridge.

nights.why: Jesus is called Immanuel, God with us. Love came close.

talk.little: Who do you like to sit close to?
talk.kids: What does it mean that God is with us?
talk.grownups: Where do you most need to know that God is with you?

nights.pray: Immanuel, thank you for coming close. Be with us at this table tonight. Amen.
nights.do: Squeeze into one spot together, like a couch or the floor. Say together: God is with us.

nights.why: Jesus was born in a humble place. God's love comes to ordinary homes like ours.

talk.little: Where do babies sleep?
talk.kids: Why do you think God chose a manger and not a palace?
talk.grownups: How can our home make room for Jesus this week?

nights.pray: Jesus, you came to a humble place. Make room in our hearts and our home for you. Amen.
nights.do: Make a small manger from things at home, like a box and a cloth, and set it where everyone can see it.

nights.why: The first people to hear the news were shepherds working at night. God's light found them.

talk.little: What did the shepherds see?
talk.kids: Why do you think God told shepherds first?
talk.grownups: Who are the overlooked people God wants to reach through you?

nights.pray: God, thank you that your good news is for everyone. Help us share it with joy. Amen.
nights.do: Turn the lights low, then switch them all on at once. Talk about how the shepherds felt.

nights.why: Angels filled the sky with praise, and the shepherds hurried to find Jesus.

talk.little: Can you sing like an angel?
talk.kids: If you had been a shepherd, what would you have done first?
talk.grownups: What would it look like to hurry toward Jesus this Christmas?

nights.pray: Glory to you, God. Thank you for sending Jesus. Fill our home with peace tonight. Amen.
nights.do: Sing one Christmas carol together before bed. If your church has a service tonight, talk about what you hope to hear.

nights.why: Merry Christmas. The light has come, and the darkness cannot overcome it.

talk.little: Who came at Christmas?
talk.kids: What is your favorite part of the Christmas story, and why?
talk.grownups: What does it mean for you that the darkness cannot overcome the light?

nights.pray: Jesus, thank you for coming. You are our light. We love you. Amen.
nights.do: Together, look back at your wreath and name one thing you learned this Advent. Then say: the light has come.
